name: Joystick Jammers UI tokens
statusNote: Draft from P1-U01, reworked in P1-U01.3 for R102 (the language block). C01 and D05 build from this draft; every other UI task waits for the owner's G-DESIGN verdict (P1-U04), which freezes the accepted copy in art/ui/accepted/<date>/.

ink.role: Deep navy ink: outlines, text on paper, the controller's dark base

ink-raised.role: Raised surface on the ink base (controller panels in a dim room)

ink-soft.role: Muted ink text on paper (secondary labels)

paper.role: Warm paper cream: TV panels and text on ink

saffron.role: Primary accent: primary buttons, highlight bars, timer emphasis

cobalt.role: Secondary accent: links, selection, keyboard focus, numbers on paper

cobalt-deep.role: Cobalt text on paper at small sizes

red-earth.role: World colour: red dirt (backgrounds and illustration, not UI text)

danger-tint.role: Destructive secondary fill and error panels

warning-tint.role: Warning toasts and reconnecting panels (ink text)

identity.rule: Every seat gets a number and a colour. Numbers are unique in the room and carry identity for any N; colours cycle through this list in order (seat N takes colour (N-1) mod 12), so colours repeat with distinct numbers as N grows. No cap (R66). Patterns are Full (plan §2.3).
identity.numberFormat: #{n}, any number of digits, tabular figures
identity.badge: Number in the display face on the seat colour, ink outline, sticker shadow; text colour is the colour's `on` value

display.role: Event titles, headings, numbers, countdowns, room codes

fonts.fallbackNote: The bundled faces cover Latin, Latin Extended and Vietnamese. Other scripts (CJK, Arabic, Devanagari, Cyrillic, Greek…) fall back to the device's own system font, never a remote font service (R70).
fonts.subset: U+0000-024F, U+0300-036F, U+1E00-1EFF, punctuation, currency, arrows (fonts/subset.py)

tv.viewing: TV at about 3 m, sized on a 1920x1080 reference; scale every value by the output height / 1080

desk.viewing: Laptop or desktop at about 60 cm

type.displayCase: uppercase for titles and headings; sentence case for labels and buttons
type.capHeightNote: Both Barlow faces have a cap height of 700/1000 em (OS/2 sCapHeight), so each profile's minimum cap height is its minimum text size × 0.7

space.unit: the profile's unit (tv: px@1080p, desk and handheld: css-px)

layout.stickRegion: Each controller stick region spans at least 45% of the screen's long side and the full lower two-thirds in landscape (C02 tunes)

tvSafe.note: Fractions of each screen dimension: text and the QR stay inside title-safe, other chrome inside action-safe; tiles may bleed to the edge

layout.radiusNote: The control radius (buttons, fields). Since R102 it is not a uniform radius: every other element takes its corner from language.corners.

stickerShadow.note: Hard offset, never blurred; y scales with the profile like outlinePx (desk 5 px, TV about 6.7 px at 1080p)

stickerShadowOnInk.note: On ink surfaces an ink shadow vanishes; use black at 55 %

wobble.seed: a hash of the element's stable id, so each panel keeps the same edge everywhere and across reloads
wobble.appliesTo: Panel and badge outlines only. Text baselines, content boxes, hit boxes and focus rings stay straight rectangles.
wobble.note: Master §12.1: a few px at TV scale, consistent per element, never animated

language.ruling: R102 (owner POC round 1, POC1-03): hand-made rather than web-grid
takes: Non-grid, hand-made placement: free panels tilt a little and sit off a column grid, anchored to the art
Big renders as first-class elements: cut-out cars and highlight art, large, allowed to break a panel's edge
A contrasting banner behind heading type: a torn ink banner with paper type and one accent word
Compact density: tight padding and gaps, many things on one screen
Slants and high contrast that feel alive: skewed tags, rotated banners, burst ticks, ink on saffron
Colour behind some text: tags, strips and highlighter underlines behind short lines
notTaken: Copy, slogans and painted signage text
Vote cards and the voting flow
Car art and liveries (our cars are code-built, R81)

slant.seed: a hash of the element's stable id, like the wobble, so a panel keeps its tilt everywhere
slant.never: Body copy, text fields, lists and tables, focus rings, hit boxes, and the race grid's tiles stay straight

heading.note: Headings and screen titles in display type sit on it; one accent word in saffron; the banner may overhang the panel it heads

tag.note: A section label: display italic, skewed and tilted, ragged brush ends

strip.note: Colour behind one short line (a result, a status, a points value); never behind a paragraph

underline.note: A highlighter stroke under a key heading or the player's own line

ticks.note: Burst ticks either side of the one thing that matters most on a screen (the primary action or an exclamation); at most one set per screen

corners.rule: No uniform radius. Panels, banners, tags and strips are square, torn or wobbled; buttons and fields get a small radius; badges a smaller one; only status chips are pills.

placement.note: On free screens (join, lobby, pause, intermission, results) panels anchor to the art, not a column grid: they may tilt (panelTiltMaxDeg), step off alignment by offsetPx and overlap a neighbour by up to overlapPx. Lists, tables, forms, tile grids and anything a gamepad walks in order stay aligned.

density.note: Compact: panels pad by space step 4 (16 px desk, 32 px TV), rows sit 8 px apart (TV 16), section gaps are one step tighter than the old draft.

renders.cutout: Renders are cut-outs with an ink outline at least ink.outlinePx; they may break a panel's edge by up to 20% of their height
renders.where: Join, lobby, intermission, results and pause give the hero render (the player's car or a highlight) at least minScreenShare of the screen. Never behind body text; never on the race grid.
renders.sheetStandIn: renders/cruz-missile-hero.png (Spike J's L0 hero render, cut out by renders/make.py) until the renderer makes its own

gamepad.marker: A saffron chevron tab on the focused element's leading edge, so the selection reads from the couch
gamepad.lift: translateY(-2px) plus a deeper sticker shadow

edge.note: An ink hairline either side of the saffron ring: saffron alone is about 1.6:1 against paper

focus.note: Focus is always visible on keyboard and gamepad navigation; it is never removed for looks (experience direction §3)

icons.source: Lucide (ISC licence), vendored as SVG in icons/

sticker-in.does: Scale 0.6 to 1 with a slight overshoot and a 4 degree settle

reduced.does: Fade in, no scale or rotation

identify-pulse.does: About 1.5 s (master §5.2, R99): 'Cooee #7' over a transparent, high-exposure flash in the seat colour, tweened (fast attack, long decay); the seat's tile border and number badge pulse, a bright outline on the car in other tiles; the controller plays the same flash in the player's colour

reduced.does: No flash at all (POC2-15): the label shows for the same time without scale, the border holds thick, the outline shows

countdown-beat.does: Each number punches in (scale 1.4 to 1) and fades on the beat

reduced.does: Numbers swap on the beat, no scale

reflow.does: Tiles slide to their new cells when players join or leave

reduced.does: Tiles cut to their new cells

results-reveal.does: Podium cards drop in from the top, staggered by 150 ms

toast.does: Slides in 16 px and fades; stays 4 s

wreck-shake.does: A small screen shake on the wrecked player's tile only

reduced.does: No shake; the comic impact word still shows

motion.reducedMotionNote: Reduced motion removes shake, flashes, overshoot and scale, never information, controls or timing (experience direction §2)

qr.rule: Plain black-on-white code with a quiet zone of at least 4 modules on every side and nothing in the middle; error correction M; the room code sits beside it, never inside, in the display face
